SSM forensic addendum (read-only; no remote mutation): confirmed the live MCP server is on AWS SSM instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5 in us-east-1 (host ip-172-31-7-214.ec2.internal). The running container is /rebar-mcp-8db373933654-8093 (host pid 1108268), command `rebar-mcp`, started 2026-08-31T09:08:54Z. Its process environment sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` and `REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`; Docker mounts map host volume `/var/lib/docker/volumes/gerrit_mcp_tickets/_data` to `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` and `/var/lib/docker/volumes/gerrit_mcp_code/_data` to `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`. This confirms the MCP write path used a separate server-side tracker clone/volume, not the local checkout path `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`.

Remote lock inspection at 2026-09-01T06:21Z found `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets/.ticket-write.lock` present and empty, `.ticket-write.lock.d` and `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` absent, pid 49003 absent in host and container `/proc`, no compact-sweep process, and no lsof holder on the lock file. This means the stale stamp observed during the incident had already been cleaned by the time of SSM inspection; I did not clear/restart anything.

Remote Docker logs still contain the incident proof: repeated MCP write failures/warnings report `holder: host=boot-bf4c34b1-475c-4363-8ff6-aada80c3c3ab pid=49003 start=19655570 ... pid_state=live op=compact-sweep`, including `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s`. The repeated `held=` values in the same log are non-monotonic (examples: 55s, 50s, 67s, 8s, 11s, 72s, 42s, 52s, 21s, 10s, 71s, etc.) while the holder pid/start/op stay constant, matching stale owner-stamp reads rather than a live continuously-held kernel lock. Combined with the current remote absence of pid 49003 and no lsof holder, this confirms the production-side mechanism: the MCP server read its own stale server-volume `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` stamp and the old liveness diagnostic reported the dead/reused pid as `live`; the local checkout succeeded because it was a different tracker path.
